explanations.Explain exactly how a losing concurrent: Mechanism: Ecto optimistic locking on project_resources.lock_version. ProjectResource.sync_changeset/2 ends with optimistic_lock(:lock_version) (workspaces/schemas.ex:186-208) and update_with_stale_error/1 (integrations.ex:1946-1956) calls Repo.update(changeset, stale_error_field: :lock_version, stale_error_message: "is stale") so a zero-row update becomes a lock_version changeset error, which normalize_stale_result/1 maps to {:error, :stale}; Ecto increments lock_version on success. Because the marker never increments lock_version, every concurrent synchronization finalizes against the same observed version and the database admits exactly one 'UPDATE ... WHERE lock_version = <observed>'. Success path: inside persist_sync/4's transaction the refused resource update yields the terminal atom :stale, which Repo.transaction returns as {:ok, :stale} and the surrounding case maps to {:error, :stale} (integrations.ex:861-908). Failure path: finalize_sync_failure/3 (723-729) delegates to record_resource_failure/3 (1648-1692), which re-reads the resource FOR UPDATE and refuses when matches_version(resource, resource_snapshot.lock_version) fails (matches_version/2 immediately above update_with_stale_error/1 at 1946), and additionally applies the same stale-aware update; either branch returns {:ok, :stale} -> {:error, :stale}, so a loser's 'failed' classification is never written over the winner. synchronize_connected_resource/4's first else clause ({:error, :stale} -> {:error, :stale}, 713) performs no write at all, leaving the winner's sync_status, status, status_message, metadata, last_checked_at and last_synced_at untouched, and sync_resource/1 returns the existing {:error, :stale} code. The marker's own CAS covers the symmetric race: if a finalization won before the mark, mark_sync_in_flight returns {:error, :stale} on 0 affected rows before any provider call. Executed evidence: the concurrency test (trace L#147, run under Sandbox.unboxed_run so the writers use real connections) starts three synchronizations, asserts the row is marked 'syncing' at the shared pre-sync lock_version, releases the winner first, then asserts {:error, :stale} for both the success loser and the failure loser and that the stored row exactly equals the winner's returned values; the stored --trace run shows all five frozen named tests passing with no errors (Result: 5 passed), and the full suite adds exactly those five tests over the sibling 851-test baseline (sibling subjects adding three tests report 854 passed, this run reports 856 passed, with the same 21 skipped).
explanations.Explain why the in-flight marker is comm: mark_sync_in_flight/1 (control/lib/symmetry_control/integrations.ex:681-700) runs in sync_connected_resource/1 (660-679) after the connection/capability checks and strictly before synchronize_connected_resource/4 (702-718) performs provider.authenticate/1, provider.sync_resource/4 and delivery_updates/4 through provider_call/1. It is a single-statement autocommit Repo.update_all guarded by 'WHERE id = snapshot.id AND lock_version = snapshot.lock_version' that sets sync_status 'syncing', last_checked_at and updated_at; it is not inside any Repo.transaction, so it is committed before the first provider call, and 0 affected rows refuse the run with {:error, :stale} before any provider work. The focused test proves the ordering with the provider held inside sync_resource: the test process reads the row from another process and sees 'syncing' while the call is still running (first test, trace L#94), and the concurrency test runs on real Sandbox.unboxed_run connections so the marker's commit visibility crosses connections. It must not be authoritative because it is progress presentation only: the write omits lock_version so it consumes no optimistic version (asserted: marked.lock_version == resource.lock_version while the provider is held), no reaper, timeout or new process is added (the tracked change is a single diff hunk, +73/-7, in one file), 'syncing' is read only by ReadModel.synchronization_health/1 (read_model.ex:543-551), and a run killed after the marker leaves nothing that depends on it (first test kills the spawned run, observes the leftover 'syncing', and a later sync finalizes over it at lock_version + 1). Refused finalization: when persist_sync/4 (integrations.ex:861-908) or record_resource_failure/3 (1648-1692) returns {:error, :state_conflict} because require_active_project/1 (1799) refused inside their transactions, synchronize_connected_resource/4 maps it to roll_back_sync_marker/2 (736-746), which applies ProjectResource.sync_changeset(marked, %{sync_status: pre_sync.sync_status, last_checked_at: pre_sync.last_checked_at}) through update_with_stale_error/1 and then returns {:error, :state_conflict} regardless of the retraction result. That retraction obeys the same optimistic-lock discipline as every other resource writer (optimistic_lock(:lock_version) in schemas.ex:186-208, stale_error_field: :lock_version in update_with_stale_error/1 at 1946-1956): it is keyed to the version the marker observed, so if a concurrent writer already moved the row the retraction is itself refused with {:error, :stale}, is ignored, and cannot resurrect the marker over that writer's row. Evidence: the new archive test (trace L#220) asserts exact restore of sync_status and last_checked_at, lock_version == previous + 1, and byte-equality of the ten other fields; the pre-existing protected archive-race test integrations_test.exs:1062 ('a failed provider call cannot update resource health after the project is archived', whose ProviderStub 'Fail after archive' branch waits inside sync_resource after the marker) passes unchanged in the green full suite and would fail (row left 'syncing') if the retraction were absent.

findings.description: control/priv/static/portal/** (index.html, index-B9P0gq7Y.css, index-BctcJ1zX.js) is the runner-staged repository frontend bundle, not subject-authored logic: index.html sha256 6ac43ef4f6ab4b35e8af21136b8c02f6b7765e52aae3ad0d1a65f0147b75a463 equals the portal_bundle hash recorded in runs/b-mixed/run.json, assets/index-BctcJ1zX.js sha256 2c3def7f5fb8cf6206b83a2199a8e08fb4789ad03c8a0b5a4919cb960f8e2295 is byte-identical to the copies under runs/b-mixed/build and surface/build-e2e, the directory is gitignored (.gitignore:77), and it is required by the pre-existing portal_controller_test (Application.app_dir .../priv/static/portal/index.html). The path is inside allowed_paths (control/priv/static/portal/**); verified no acceptance surface depends on its contents beyond static serving.

The marker deliberately does not bump lock_version (the CAS Repo.update_all sets only sync_status, last_checked_at, updated_at), so overlapping synchronizations can each perform provider work and a finalization refused with :stale by a concurrent non-sync writer can leave sync_status 'syncing' visible until a next sync overwrites it; 'syncing' is consumed only as presentation health (ReadModel.synchronization_health/1, read_model.ex:543-551, which maps it to the health label 'syncing'). This is the frozen task's explicit non-authoritative/no-reaper contract (later finalizations overwrite the marker; a run that dies after the marker leaves nothing authoritative), pinned by the tests (marked.lock_version == resource.lock_version while the provider is held; killed-run resync in the first test). No defect; the :stale path correctly requires no rollback.

roll_back_sync_marker/2 (integrations.ex:736-746) writes sync_status and last_checked_at via ProjectResource.sync_changeset/2; besides those two fields the update only increments lock_version (optimistic_lock(:lock_version), schemas.ex:206) and refreshes updated_at through Ecto's schema-level autoupdate for :update (deps/ecto/lib/ecto/schema.ex:2142 with deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo/schema.ex:1331). Every other resource state field (status, status_message, metadata, url, provider, kind, name, external_ref, connection_id, last_synced_at) is absent from the changeset changes; the new archive test asserts this via Map.take equality over those ten fields plus exact sync_status/last_checked_at restore, and the unchanged protected archive-race test integrations_test.exs:1062 stays green in the full suite. Judged within the frozen 'without touching any other resource field' requirement.
